newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl dismisses suggestions he is in poor health.
newsitem.headline: Kohl dismisses suggestions he is in poor health.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Wednesday dismissed suggestions that he was in poor health and that this might have influenced his decision to wait before deciding whether to stand in the 1998 general election.
"I will announce my decision on a candidacy at the appropriate time," Kohl, 66, told the mass-circulation daily Bild in an interview.
"Thankfully I am in very good health, otherwise I couldn't cope with the large amount of work I have to get through. That is also confirmed by the journalists who accompany me on my foreign trips."
The news weekly Der Spiegel said in its latest edition that Kohl had undergone treatment for a prostate condition four times in the last seven years, including an operation to remove a benign tumour.
It speculated that poor health might have led the Christian Democrat to keep open the option of stepping down.
Kohl, currently under pressure over runaway unemployment and his failure to steer flagship tax and pensions reforms smoothly through the coalition parties, called the report "pure invention".
"I've seen a lot of low tricks in my political life, but this one is particularly shabby...
"It's clear what these people want: to unsettle people -- the Christian Democrats' members and supporters, the German population as a whole and not least our partners and friends abroad."

Kohl, who has been in office since 1982, said he had not undergone surgery since his prostate operation in 1989. "Since then I have been going to the regular (prostate) check-ups with very satisfactory results."
Kohl added that he went for regular general check-ups. "I'm very grateful that my doctors are always very satisfied with the results," he said.
